1.1/O1.name: Commutative
1.1/O1.note: The order of two terms or two factors may be swapped.

1.1/O1.name: Associative
1.1/O1.note: The grouping may be changed; the order may not.

1.1/O1.name: Distributive
1.1/O1.note: Since $b-c$ means $b+(-c)$, the subtraction form is the same statement. Read right to left, it takes out a common factor.

1.1/O2.name: Substitution
1.1/O2.statement: Replace each variable with its value, then evaluate.

1.1/O2.name: Negatives go in parentheses
1.1/O2.note: Substituting without parentheses gives $-3^{2}=-9$, a different number.

1.1/O3.name: Order of operations
1.1/O3.statement: Parentheses, then exponents, then $\times$ and $\div$ left to right, then $+$ and $-$ left to right.

1.1/O3.name: What counts as grouping
1.1/O3.statement: Parentheses, the fraction bar, and the radical all group.
1.1/O3.note: Everything above a fraction bar is divided by everything below it.

1.1/O3.name: Exponents and the minus sign
1.1/O3.note: The exponent applies to 9 unless parentheses place the minus inside the base. The same distinction makes $b^{2}-4ac$ come out right in the quadratic formula in 1.7.

1.1/O4.name: Order on the number line
1.1/O4.statement: $a<b$ means $a$ lies to the left of $b$.

1.1/O4.name: Comparing across forms
1.1/O4.statement: Write both numbers in one form first: $\tfrac{3}{8}=0.375$, so $\tfrac{3}{8}<0.4$.

1.1/O5.name: Interval notation
1.1/O5.statement: $(a,b)$ excludes both ends, $[a,b]$ includes both, $[a,b)$ includes only the left.

1.1/O5.name: On the graph
1.1/O5.statement: A hollow dot excludes the endpoint, a solid dot includes it.

1.2/O1.name: Base and exponent
1.2/O1.statement: $a^{n}$ is $a$ used as a factor $n$ times. $a$ is the base, $n$ the exponent.

1.2/O1.name: Where the minus sits
1.2/O1.note: In the second, only the 2 is raised.

1.2/O1.name: Sign of a power of a negative
1.2/O1.statement: An even power is positive, an odd power is negative.

1.2/O2.name: Power rule
1.2/O2.note: A power of a power multiplies.

1.2/O3.name: Polynomial vocabulary
1.2/O3.statement: term, coefficient, degree of a term, degree of the polynomial, leading coefficient

1.2/O3.name: Degree
1.2/O3.statement: The degree of a polynomial is the highest degree among its terms.

1.2/O3.name: Leading coefficient
1.2/O3.statement: In $-4x^{3}+7x^{2}-x+9$ the degree is 3 and the leading coefficient is $-4$.
1.2/O3.note: The sign belongs to the coefficient.

1.2/O3.name: By number of terms
1.2/O3.statement: one term monomial, two binomial, three trinomial

1.2/O4.name: Like terms
1.2/O4.statement: Same variable raised to the same exponent: $5x^{2}$ and $2x^{2}$ are like, $5x^{2}$ and $3x$ are not.

1.2/O4.name: Adding
1.2/O4.statement: Add the coefficients of like terms; the exponent does not change.

1.2/O5.name: Distribute term by term
1.2/O5.statement: Every term of the first factor multiplies every term of the second.

1.2/O6.name: Building the polynomial
1.2/O6.statement: Turn the described quantity into an expression, then evaluate it at the stated value.

1.3/O1.name: What the GCF is
1.3/O1.statement: The greatest common factor of the coefficients, times the lowest power of each variable common to every term.

1.3/O1.name: Worked example
1.3/O1.note: $6$ divides 12 and 18; $x^{2}$ is the lowest power present.

1.3/O1.name: Check by expanding
1.3/O1.statement: Multiply the factored form out; it must equal the original polynomial.

1.3/O1.name: Completely
1.3/O1.statement: Nothing common may remain inside the bracket.
1.3/O1.note: $6x(2x^{2}-3x)$ is a true factorisation but not complete: $x$ still divides both terms inside.

1.3/O2.name: Factoring $x^{2}+bx+c$
1.3/O2.note: For $x^{2}+7x+12$, $2\cdot 6=12$ but $2+6\ne 7$, so $2$ and $6$ do not work.

1.3/O2.name: Reading the signs
1.3/O2.statement: $c>0$: $p$ and $q$ share the sign of $b$.  $c<0$: they have opposite signs.

1.3/O3.name: Product and sum
1.3/O3.statement: Find two numbers with product $ac$ and sum $b$.

1.3/O3.name: Always check
1.3/O3.note: $3$ and $1$ placed as $(2x+3)(x+1)$ give $5x$; placed as $(2x+1)(x+3)$ they give $7x$.

1.4/O1.name: Factor first
1.4/O1.statement: Factor the numerator and the denominator completely, then cancel.

1.4/O1.name: Only factors cancel
1.4/O1.note: The bar groups the whole numerator; a 3 cannot be cancelled against one term of it.

1.4/O1.name: Restrictions
1.4/O1.statement: The denominator may never be zero; exclude the values that make it so.

1.4/O2.name: Multiplying
1.4/O2.statement: Factor everything, cancel across the fraction bar, then multiply what is left.

1.5/O1.name: Negative exponent
1.5/O1.note: A negative exponent means a reciprocal, not a negative answer: $2^{-3}=\tfrac{1}{8}$.

1.5/O1.name: The rules still hold
1.5/O1.statement: Product, quotient and power rules work for negative integers too.

1.6/O1.name: Addition property
1.6/O1.statement: Adding the same quantity to both sides keeps the equation true.

1.6/O1.name: Multiplication property
1.6/O1.statement: Multiplying both sides by the same non-zero quantity keeps it true.

1.6/O1.name: Solving for the variable
1.6/O1.statement: Collect the variable on one side and the numbers on the other, then divide by the coefficient.

1.6/O1.name: Check
1.6/O1.statement: Substitute the answer back into the original equation.

1.6/O2.name: Clear the fractions
1.6/O2.statement: Multiply both sides by the LCD of every denominator.
1.6/O2.note: Every term, including the ones that are not fractions.

1.6/O3.name: Solving for one letter among several
1.6/O3.statement: Treat the other letters as if they were numbers.

1.6/O3.name: When the target appears twice
1.6/O3.statement: Collect its terms on one side and factor it out, then divide by the bracket.

1.6/O4.name: Translating a word problem
1.6/O4.statement: Name the unknown, write the equation the words describe, solve it, then read the answer back against the question.

1.7/O1.name: Standard form first
1.7/O1.statement: $ax^{2}+bx+c=0$ — everything on one side, zero on the other.

1.7/O1.name: Zero-product property
1.7/O1.note: $AB=6$ gives no such conclusion: the product must be $0$.

1.7/O1.name: Worked example
1.7/O1.note: The roots are the opposites of the numbers in the brackets.

1.7/O2.name: Reading a, b, c
1.7/O2.note: The signs belong to the coefficients.

1.7/O2.name: Discriminant
1.7/O2.statement: $b^{2}-4ac$ positive gives two real solutions, zero gives one, negative gives none.
The formula solves any quadratic, including those that do not factor.
1.7/O2.name: Applies to every quadratic

1.1/O6.name: Definition of absolute value
1.1/O6.statement: $|a|$ is the distance from $a$ to 0 on the number line.

1.1/O6.name: The bars group
1.1/O6.note: Evaluate inside first. $|3|-|7|=-4$ is a different calculation and a different answer.

1.1/O6.name: Where the minus sits
1.1/O6.note: The bars apply only to what is inside them: $|-5|=5$, and the outside minus then gives $-5$.
